$comment: One shard of the signal-lens catalogue. DATA, never loaded whole into an agent context. Validate with: python3 scripts/validate_catalogue.py

signals.name: Product configuration
signals.definition: The subject assembles a specific specification of the product rather than viewing a preset one - a configurator, plan builder, bundle picker, room or system planner, or a quote builder. Qualifying condition: at least one configuration option is moved off its default and the resulting state is carried to a summary, price, save, or share step.
signals.question_answered: Has the buyer moved from 'is this the right category' to 'this is the exact thing I would buy', and what specification would they buy?

capability_ladder.how: Emit configuration_step_completed with the option key and chosen value from the configurator you already run - the configurator holds this state in memory to price the item and then discards it on unload; write it to an event instead
requires: tag manager or app-level analytics
an existing configurator, plan table, or bundle picker
capability_ladder.gives: The specification itself, not just 'someone used the configurator'

capability_ladder.how: Persist the configuration server-side against a resumable key so a returning subject picks it back up, which also yields abandon step and repeat-configuration count
requires: a backend store and a durable first-party key
capability_ladder.gives: Cross-session continuity and the exact step where specification stalls

capability_ladder.how: Join saved configurations to quotes and orders in the commerce or CRM backend so you learn which option combinations convert and which are dead ends
requires: order or opportunity records keyed to the same subject
capability_ladder.gives: Converts a behavioural signal into a merchandising and pricing input

access_conditions: No third party is involved at any rung; this signal is obtainable entirely from surfaces you already own

freshness.note: A configuration is a live specification while the requirement stands; it decays as the buyer either orders, respecifies, or drops the project.

false_positives: Employee or agency testing of the configurator after a release
Recreational configuring - car, PC and kitchen configurators are used as entertainment by people with no budget
Competitor reconnaissance on option availability and price break points
A specifier or proxy researcher configuring on behalf of the person who will actually buy
An existing customer configuring a replacement part or an add-on to something already owned
Student or hobbyist coursework

signals.name: Compatibility check
signals.definition: The subject tests the product against something they already own or are bound by - an installed system or version, a device or vehicle, a physical space, a standard, a service region. Qualifying condition: a fitment, serviceability, or integration lookup is executed carrying a specific identifier of the incumbent thing (model, version, registration, postcode, named system), and a pass or fail result is returned.
signals.question_answered: Is the buyer testing us against a constraint they already own, and which constraint is the one that could kill the deal?

capability_ladder.how: Log the input and the result of the compatibility lookup you already serve - the delivery-postcode checker, the 'will it fit my vehicle' selector, the version-requirements table, the integrations directory search. The result is already computed server-side; persist the pair instead of only rendering it
requires: an existing fitment, serviceability, or integration lookup
capability_ladder.gives: The named incumbent constraint, which is the field sales actually needs

capability_ladder.how: Treat each integration or compatibility documentation page as a check keyed on the third-party system named on that page, so you capture the other half of the buyer's stack without owning a lookup tool
requires: one page per named system and pageview tracking
capability_ladder.gives: Coverage for companies with no configurator, at lower precision

capability_ladder.how: Aggregate failed checks into a standing demand register - which constraint fails most often, in which region, at what rate - and route that to product and partnerships rather than to sales
requires: result stored with the failing value, not just a boolean
capability_ladder.gives: Turns lost buyers into a ranked roadmap input; also the only honest way to size a market you currently cannot serve

access_conditions: A serviceability check that takes a full address rather than a postal district collects more personal data than the answer requires; take the coarsest input that returns a correct result

freshness.note: The intent decays over weeks, but a recorded failed constraint is a durable fact about that subject and should be kept after the intent has gone.

false_positives: A competitor or analyst mapping which systems, regions, or vehicle models you support
An implementation partner or consultant checking on behalf of a client who is the real buyer
An existing customer confirming an upgrade or migration path rather than making a new purchase
Crawlers, scrapers and LLM agents hitting integration and compatibility pages, which are unusually attractive to automated retrieval
A job applicant researching the stack before an interview
A user checking the fitment of a consumable for equipment they already own

signals.name: Requirement formation
signals.definition: The subject expresses what the solution must satisfy, as a constraint rather than a preference - filters applied and kept across views, a must-have checklist, requirement fields on a form, a published specification or scope of works, or a stated threshold in a sales or support conversation. Qualifying condition: at least one requirement is expressed as a value, threshold, standard, or exclusion attributable to the subject.
signals.question_answered: What must be true for this buyer to say yes, and can we satisfy it as we are today?

capability_ladder.how: Persist the facet filters your catalogue or directory already exposes as named requirement key-value pairs on the subject, keeping only the filters that survive more than one view - a filter applied and immediately removed is browsing, a filter carried across views is a requirement
requires: a filterable catalogue, directory, or search UI
capability_ladder.gives: Machine-readable constraints with no new form and no extra question asked of the buyer

capability_ladder.how: Add two or three structured requirement fields to the form you already run, replacing an open 'tell us about your project' box, and mark each as must-have or nice-to-have
requires: an existing enquiry, quote, or signup form
capability_ladder.gives: Requirements you can score against your own capability table, rather than free text nobody parses

capability_ladder.how: Extract requirement statements from sales notes, support tickets, and supplied specification documents into the same key-value shape, so a requirement stated on a call ranks alongside one typed into a filter
requires: CRM or ticket text access and an agreed requirement vocabulary
capability_ladder.gives: The only rung that catches requirements from buyers who never touch your website

min_data.note: Requirement keys are only comparable once a controlled vocabulary exists. Below roughly 20 agreed keys the extract at rung 3 produces synonyms rather than signal.

access_conditions: Free-text sales and support notes are where special-category detail most often enters a CRM; extract only against an agreed requirement vocabulary and never pass raw note text into a scoring or audience pipeline

freshness.note: Requirements outlive a browsing session and often outlive the vendor shortlist; they die when the project is funded elsewhere or shelved.

false_positives: Filters used as a browsing convenience rather than a constraint, especially price filters set to explore a range
Requirements copied verbatim from a template or an incumbent supplier's specification, which describe the incumbent rather than the buyer's real need
A non-decision-maker stating requirements that the economic buyer will overrule
A procurement-mandated specification written to justify a supplier already chosen
An analyst, consultant, or student assembling a requirements matrix for a report
Aspirational must-haves that are dropped as soon as they carry a price

signals.name: Eligibility check
signals.definition: The subject supplies facts about themselves, for the stated purpose of the check, to learn whether they qualify - address serviceability, minimum or maximum thresholds such as company size or fleet count, licence or accreditation status, trade, student, or nonprofit status, or an affordability pre-check. Qualifying condition: the subject declares the qualifying facts for this purpose and a pass, fail, or refer result is returned against their record. Facts inferred from behaviour rather than declared are out of scope.
signals.question_answered: Can this buyer actually be served or approved, and if not, exactly what disqualified them?

capability_ladder.how: Store the outcome of the eligibility gate you already operate - the serviceability postcode box, the 'are you VAT registered', the minimum-order or minimum-headcount screen - as a three-state result on the subject rather than as a page that silently redirects
requires: an existing eligibility or serviceability gate
capability_ladder.gives: A pass/fail/refer state, and the population of people you turn away, which almost nobody counts

capability_ladder.how: Add a coded decline reason so a fail becomes actionable - out of area, below threshold, wrong accreditation - and offer the qualifying path on the result screen
requires: a reason-code vocabulary agreed with the team that owns the rule
capability_ladder.gives: Turns a rejection into either a routed referral or a measured gap

capability_ladder.how: Verify declared facts against an authoritative register the subject has authorised you to query - a public licence or company register, or a regulated bureau check where one applies - and store only the verdict, not the underlying report
requires: an authorisation record from the subject
a lawful basis and, for bureau checks, a permissible purpose
capability_ladder.gives: A verified rather than asserted eligibility state, at materially higher legal cost

access_conditions: Rungs 1 and 2 need only notice. Rung 3 changes the permission axis, not the availability axis: a check performed against a consumer credit bureau is a consumer report and requires a permissible purpose, adverse-action handling, and retention limits, none of which the subject's willingness to be checked supplies on its own
Store the verdict, not the evidence. A decline reason code belongs in the servicing record and must never be copied into a marketing attribute, audience, or lookalike seed

Where an eligibility route exists only for applicants with a health condition, a disability, or a benefit entitlement, the fact that a subject took that route must not be retained as a segment - see restricted.eligibility_route_special_category_inference
signals.terms_note: Bureau-backed affordability and credit pre-checks are regulated consumer-reporting activity in the US and equivalent regimes elsewhere; the declared-facts variant described here is not, and the two must not be scored as one signal.

freshness.note: A pass is a durable fact for as long as the underlying rule and the subject's circumstances hold; the intent it accompanies decays much faster than the eligibility state does.

false_positives: Curiosity checks - people test serviceability for an address they are only considering, particularly during a house search
An agent, broker, or family member running the check with someone else's details
Repeated attempts with altered values to find the threshold, which reads as several qualified subjects and is one unqualified one
A trade or nonprofit status claimed to unlock a discount by someone not entitled to it
An existing customer re-checking eligibility for a second site or vehicle
Automated form submissions and LLM agents completing gates to reach the content behind them

signals.name: Diagnostic tool use
signals.definition: The subject submits an asset they own or operate to a tool that inspects it and returns findings - a site, security, or performance scan, a network or speed test, an energy or insulation audit, a fault-code lookup, a soil, water, or emissions test, a compliance or tax checker. Qualifying condition: an identifiable asset is submitted and a findings payload with a severity or score is produced against it. Tools whose output is a statement about a person's body or health are out of scope and are not detectable signals here.
signals.question_answered: Has the buyer had a specific defect in their own environment quantified, and how bad is the finding?

capability_ladder.how: Store the findings of the free checker you already publish against the asset identifier, not just the fact that someone ran it - the severity of the worst finding is the signal, and it is thrown away by almost every free-tool implementation
requires: an existing audit, scan, calculator, or checker
capability_ladder.gives: A severity-ranked queue instead of an undifferentiated list of tool users

capability_ladder.how: Keep the run history per asset so you can compute the delta between runs - a subject who re-runs and finds the problem unchanged is a subject who has failed to fix it themselves
requires: asset-keyed storage across sessions
capability_ladder.gives: Distinguishes a fixed problem from a persistent one, which is the difference between a closed need and an open one

capability_ladder.how: Where the subject connects the asset directly rather than pasting an identifier, monitor it on a schedule and treat a newly appearing high-severity finding as the trigger, so the signal fires when the problem appears rather than when the buyer remembers your tool
requires: an authorised connection to the asset
an explicit monitoring consent and a revocation path
capability_ladder.gives: Shifts the signal from pull to push; upgrades permission from notice to explicit consent

access_conditions: Scan only an asset the requester controls or has authorised. Unsolicited scanning of third-party infrastructure can constitute unauthorised access under computer-misuse statutes regardless of how benign the scan is, and asserting ownership in a form field does not make it true - rate-limit and log the assertion
Findings about a live asset can themselves be an exposure. Do not publish, resell, or index a findings payload that names a third party's vulnerability
signals.terms_note: Diagnostic output about a named third party's asset is materially different from output about the requester's own; the second is a service, the first can be a disclosure.

freshness.note: The intent decays quickly, but an unremediated high-severity finding stays true until the next run contradicts it; re-run the asset before treating an old finding as current.

false_positives: An agency, consultant, or reseller running the tool on a client's or a prospect's asset - the dominant archetype for any free scanner, and the runner is never the buyer
A competitor benchmarking your tool's output against their own
Curiosity runs by an owner with no budget and no intention to remediate
Automated or scripted runs, including LLM agents completing a scan on a user's behalf, which inflate volume and carry no contact
Internal QA and demo runs by your own staff
Someone scanning an asset they do not own - a competitor's domain, a landlord's building, a rival's fleet

signals.name: Measurement taken
signals.definition: The subject supplies a dimensional measurement of the thing the purchase must fit - a room, opening, roof, floor area, rack, vehicle bay, or an object or garment size - for the stated purpose of checking fit or producing a quote. Qualifying condition: at least one numeric measurement with a unit is recorded against the subject or the site, declared by the subject or captured by a surveyor with their agreement. Measurement of a person's body geometry derived from a photo, video, or scan is out of scope; see restricted.body_measurement_health_inference.
signals.question_answered: Has this buyer got as far as measuring, and does what they measured actually fit what we sell?

capability_ladder.how: Turn the measurement you already ask for into structured numeric fields with a unit. Most quote forms and order notes already contain dimensions, typed into a free-text box where nothing can read them - three numeric fields and a unit selector is a one-afternoon change
requires: an existing quote, enquiry, or order form
capability_ladder.gives: Machine-comparable dimensions and, immediately, a fits/does-not-fit flag against your own catalogue range

capability_ladder.how: Score each measurement against the catalogue on submission and tell the subject the answer, storing both the measurement and the verdict; a measurement that falls outside your range is a routing decision, not a lead
requires: catalogue dimension ranges in a queryable form
capability_ladder.gives: Converts a lead-capture field into a qualification gate, and counts the demand you cannot serve

capability_ladder.how: Capture surveyed measurements from the field system your installers or surveyors already use and write them back to the same fields, so a measurement taken on site ranks alongside one typed on the website
requires: an export or connector from the field-service or survey system
capability_ladder.gives: The measurement that actually governs the order, taken by someone competent to take it

access_conditions: Collect the dimension, not the person. A garment or fit measurement typed in by the subject for sizing is a declared attribute; the same number derived from a photograph or a body scan is biometric processing and is excluded from this catalogue as an implementable signal
Do not retain a series of body measurements for the same person over time as a profile attribute. A trend in body measurement is the shortest path from a sizing form to a health inference
signals.terms_note: Declared dimensions are ordinary personal data. Scan-derived body geometry is not, and the two must never share a field.

freshness.note: A room does not change size. The measurement stays true; the intent attached to it does not, so score the recency of the submission separately from the validity of the number.

false_positives: A measurement taken for a project that is being costed but not yet approved or funded
A tenant, occupant, or family member measuring a property they cannot authorise work on
A tradesperson or specifier measuring on behalf of a client who is the actual buyer
Estimated rather than measured numbers - round figures typed to get past a required field
A measurement submitted to compare against an incumbent supplier's quote with no intention of switching
An existing customer measuring a second room or unit, which is expansion rather than acquisition
